title: Immigration: Earned Settlement
speaker: Shockat Adam (Leicester South) (Ind)
text: In her statement, the Home Secretary used the word “fair”, or different iterations of it, 20 times. She said that her own parents left a place where “power was often arbitrary,” and the “dice were always loaded”, and they came here because they would be “treated fairly.” Now, a worker earning £40,000, who came here legally, paid their taxes and played their part, has been moved from five to 10 years, halfway through. Is changing the rules mid-game fair, or is that exactly what loaded dice look like?

title: Global Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law Sanctions Regulations 2026
speaker: Baroness Foster of Oxton (Con)
text: May I just bring to the attention of the Minister a press release that came out on 8 September, a week after Sir Keir Starmer resigned? It read: “UK to bring forward new powers to respond to moral emergency in Palestine, and target illegal settlement activity in the West Bank to protect the viability of a two-state solution”. I will happily give this document to the Minister when he has completed his response.

title: Topical Questions
speaker: Sonia Kumar (Dudley) (Lab)
text: Over 60% of people in prison have speech, language or communication needs. Effective rehabilitation must be holistic. To prevent reoffending and provide support, it is paramount that we address not only the offending behaviour, but the underlying communication, health, education and social needs. What steps is my hon. Friend the Minister taking to ensure that access to speech and language therapists and other allied health professionals is available in prison?

title: Health: HIV
speaker: Lord Cashman (Non-Afl)
text: My Lords, I refer to my register of interests, particularly as a patron of the Terrence Higgins Trust. I congratulate the Government on their HIV Action Plan for England, 2025 to 2030—and previous Governments. This is an example of what we can achieve when we work together across the political spectrum. However, can the Minister say how we will connect with the 5,000 people who are currently living with diagnosed HIV but not accessing treatment? These people are at risk of becoming seriously ill—indeed, some already have. I look forward to the Minister’s reply on this urgent issue.

title: Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency: Business Plan 2026-27
speaker: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Transport (Justin Madders)
text: I am pleased to announce the publication of the 2026 to 2027 business plan for the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency. DVSA’s business plan sets out the key business priorities the agency will deliver, including any significant changes it plans to make to its services, and performance indicators by which its performance will be assessed. This plan allows service users and members of the public to understand DVSA’s plans for delivering its core services and managing its finances. The business plan will be available electronically on www.gov.uk and a copy will be placed in the Libraries of both Houses. [HCWS476]

title: Shabir Ahmed
speaker: Viscount Goschen (Con)
text: My Lords, on 15 October, in your Lordships’ House, my noble friend Lady Monckton asked the Minister: “How many of this cohort” of foreign national offenders “who are liable to deportation remain in the United Kingdom due to Article 8 claims and human rights claims?”.—[Official Report, 15/10/26; col. 337.] The Minister, the noble Lord, Lord Lemos, answered that that information was available but not yet in a form to be published. I wonder if the noble Lord could update the House on that.

title: UK-EU Summit
speaker: The Earl of Kinnoull (CB)
text: My Lords, paragraph 53 of the joint statement discusses mutual recognition of qualifications. The news was rather disappointing in that only architects appear to be nearing the finishing post, but the paragraph refers to “other professions”. Can the Leader tell us what the other professions under discussion are and give us some idea as to the likely timing of successful arrival for them as well?

title: Access to Legal Services
speaker: Madam Deputy Speaker (Judith Cummins)
text: We now come to the Select Committee statement on behalf of the Justice Committee. Catherine Atkinson will speak for up to 10 minutes, during which no interventions may be taken. At the conclusion of the statement, Members may ask questions on the subject of the statement. These should be brief questions, not full speeches.
